cover.headline: A war windfall priced as if it will last: initiate with SELL
cover.lead: GNFC is India's only TDI maker and a debt-free state company with ~₹5,207 cr of treasury (₹354 a share). Since the US-Iran war began in late February 2026, chemical prices have spiked: chemicals EBIT was ₹463 cr in Q4FY26 and ₹425 cr in Q1FY27, against ~₹150 cr a quarter before, and the stock is up ~65% from its March low. We think most of that is a windfall: GNFC itself says global TDI capacity exceeds demand and that the war "can go either side". We value GNFC the way the street does, on **P/E of Sep-28E earnings**, at **7.5x** (its own 8.0x ex-trough forward median cut by the 7% sector de-rating). That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** The cash is real, but the market has never given GNFC full credit for it, and the state decides how it is spent. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}} (the war premium lasts into FY28); bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The war is doing the work
arguments.p: TDI rose from ₹168k a tonne (Q3FY26) to ₹255k (Q1FY27) and every spread GNFC tracks widened. The same war lifted fuel oil (+76% QoQ) and gas (+64%) costs and forced acetic acid, ethyl acetate and part of TDI to shut. Chemicals margin was 13% in the nine months before the war and 27-31% since. We assume it fades to 16-17%.

arguments.h: Strip out the war and earnings are flat
arguments.p: Our Sep-28E EPS of ₹55.2 equals FY26's ₹55.0 and is well below the TTM ₹70.6. New ammonium nitrate and nitric acid capacity (mid-2027) and a coal-fired steam plant help; prices normalising, a planned April-2027 shutdown and lower treasury income hurt. FY24-25 EPS was ₹34-41.

The segment lost ₹187 cr in FY26 and ₹85 cr in Q1FY27. A higher urea energy norm adds ~₹49 cr a year (plus ~₹61 cr of arrears in Q2FY27), but the fixed-cost revision has not come and management sees "almost no chance" of urea profits without it. We model losses of ₹120-150 cr a year.

arguments.h: The cash is real, but it is not yours
arguments.p: ₹2,410 cr of the treasury is lent to a state finance company at ~7.25%; a ₹7,000-8,000 cr BPA/phenol idea is under study; GNFC has had four MDs since Feb-2025. At ₹604 the market pays 7.1x operating earnings net of cash; at the March-2026 low it paid almost nothing. Our DCF (₹877) is the value only if the cash came back to shareholders.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): chemical margins after the July shutdowns, the ~₹61 cr energy-norm arrears and how much of the Q1 inventory was sold at war-time prices.
The Middle East conflict and oil (Brent ~US$103 on 29-Sep-2026): a ceasefire would cut both GNFC's prices and its fuel costs, and probably the former faster.
Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates (not announced by 30-Sep-2026) and any urea fixed-cost revision.
Board decision on BPA, polyols and the 350 KTPA acetic acid plant, expected by end-2026.
WNA-III, AN melt-II and the ammonia loop around mid-2027; planned Bharuch shutdown in April 2027; China/Japan/Korea TDI anti-dumping duty expires in September 2027.

sections.title: A state-owned chemical complex with a regulated fertiliser plant attached

blocks.p: GNFC runs two integrated complexes in Gujarat: Bharuch (since 1982) and Dahej (TDI-II, since 2014). It turns fuel oil, natural gas, coal, toluene, benzene and methanol into ammonia and syngas, and those into fertilisers and about a dozen bulk chemicals. Fertilisers (neem-coated urea and ANP) are 36% of revenue but sold at government-fixed prices with a subsidy; chemicals are 63% of revenue and sold at import-parity prices on one- to three-month contracts. A small IT division, (n)Code Solutions, makes up "Others". The Government of Gujarat (through Gujarat State Investments) and GSFC own 41.3%.

blocks.callout: **Corporate actions:** one buyback (Dec-2023, ₹770 a share, ₹653 cr); no bonus, split or equity raise in the last decade. Dividends: ₹10 (FY22), ₹30 (FY23), ~₹16.5 (FY24), ₹18 (FY25) and ₹21 (FY26, paid 18-Sep-2026). Management said in May-2026 that no new buyback is "in the pipeline".

sections.title: China sets the price of almost everything GNFC sells; the war lifted it for now

blocks.p: GNFC's chemicals are commodities. TDI, aniline, acetic acid and methanol trade at one Asian price, and China, with plants several times GNFC's size running on cheap coal, is the marginal supplier. GNFC prices at import parity (the landed cost of imports, including any anti-dumping duty), so its realisations rise and fall with Chinese prices and the rupee. Between FY22 and FY26 its TDI price fell from ₹229k a tonne (FY23) to ₹173k, its aniline-benzene spread from ₹77k to ₹44k and its acetic acid-methanol spread from ₹45k (FY22) to ₹7k. Then the US-Iran war, from late February 2026, disrupted Gulf supply and shipping: TDI jumped to ₹255k a tonne in Q1FY27 and every spread GNFC tracks widened, while fuel oil (+76% QoQ) and gas (+64%) costs also jumped.

blocks.callout: **So what:** this is a cyclical commodity business sitting under a structural Chinese overhang. The war has pushed prices up, but GNFC itself says global TDI capacity exceeds demand. When the war premium fades, prices revert towards Chinese cash costs, as they did in FY24-25. We treat the Q4FY26-Q1FY27 margins as a spike, not a new level.

sections.title: Chemicals: a good TDI franchise in a bad neighbourhood, now enjoying a war

blocks.p: Chemicals earned ₹913 cr of EBIT on ₹4,899 cr of revenue in FY26 (18.6%), but ₹463 cr of that came in the war-hit March quarter; the first nine months earned ₹450 cr (13.2%), close to FY24-25 (11.5-13.6%). TDI is the core: GNFC is the only producer in South Asia, makes ~57 kt a year across two plants (TDI-II at 77% utilisation in FY26) and sells ~60% of India's needs. In Q1FY27 revenue rose to ₹1,569 cr and EBIT to ₹425 cr (27.1%) on record prices, even though acetic acid (6-May to 1-Aug), ethyl acetate and part of TDI were shut because the feedstock cost more than the product was worth, and sales lagged production so inventory built up.

pair.title: Chemicals EBIT by quarter: ₹136 cr to ₹463 cr
Fuel oil and gas costs jumped ~65-75% in Q1FY27

bullets: **TDI economics:** management said in Aug-2025 that TDI-II "does not fully recover" its fixed costs at recent prices. The coal-fired steam and power plant (CCPP, ₹613 cr) was supplying steam by the August 2026 call and should cut TDI-II costs by ₹30-40k a tonne at current gas and coal prices. That fixes part of the cost problem; it does not fix the price problem.
**Aniline:** uneconomic on its own against Chinese aniline made with coal-based hydrogen at 7-8x the scale; GNFC mostly processes it for other companies on a fixed margin.

**Acetic acid and methanol:** GNFC's methanol plants have been idle since Nov-2024 because gas is too expensive; it buys methanol or acetic acid, whichever is cheaper, to keep ethyl acetate running. Spreads were ₹7-12k a tonne through FY26.
**Ammonium nitrate and nitric acid:** the growth leg. AN prices rose ~20% QoQ in Q4FY26; AN melt-II and WNA-III double AN capacity from mid-2027.
**Technical-grade urea:** a quiet winner. When the war cut diesel-exhaust-fluid supply in March 2026, GNFC doubled TGU output; TGU was "one of the significant contributors" to Q1 profit.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we model chemicals revenue +18% in FY27E (Q1 at war prices, ~₹1,400 cr a quarter after), −10% in FY28E (prices normalise; the April-2027 Bharuch shutdown) and +18% in FY29E (first full year of the new AN and nitric acid capacity). EBIT margin 19.5% / 16% / 17%: well below the last two quarters (27-31%) and the FY22 peak (37%), but above the FY24-25 trough (12.5%) because of CCPP savings and new capacity. Sep-28E chemicals EBIT of ₹938 cr compares with ₹665 cr in FY25 and ₹913 cr in FY26.

sections.title: Fertilisers: regulated, loss-making for six years, waiting on Delhi

blocks.p: GNFC makes neem-coated urea (reassessed capacity 637 kt; ~620 kt sold in FY26) and ANP, a 20:20:0 nitrogen-phosphate fertiliser (172,995 t). Neither price is set by the market. Urea sells at a fixed farm price and the government pays the rest of a "normative" cost under the New Urea Policy: gas at the pooled price, energy up to a plant-specific norm (Gcal per tonne) and a fixed-cost element. ANP gets a per-kg Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) set each season. In FY26 the segment had revenue of ₹2,764 cr, including ₹1,982 cr of subsidy, and lost ₹187 cr: about ₹147 cr on urea and ₹40 cr on ANP.

A fixed-cost revision is the upside (our bull case halves the loss); a war-driven gas squeeze or a weak Rabi NBS is the downside. Management's own line, May-2026: until norms are revised "we see almost no chance in case of urea".

sections.title: Projects: ₹2,800 cr of sensible brownfield capex, and a much bigger idea on the table

blocks.p: For the first time since TDI-II, GNFC is spending real money. Four projects worth ~₹2,800 cr were under way at Q1FY27, of which ~₹1,300 cr had been spent; the company expects ₹1,500-1,800 cr of capex in FY27 and the remaining ~₹1,500 cr "over the next 2 years", plus a ₹480-500 cr boiler. All four are brownfield, built on GNFC's own ammonia and nitric acid, and sell into a market India imports (ammonium nitrate). Management's rough guide: +₹1,200-1,500 cr of revenue and +₹500-600 cr of contribution (revenue less variable costs) "at current prognosis", i.e. at war-time prices.

bullets: **Under consideration:** BPA (150 KTPA) and polyols (100 KTPA) at Dahej, and a 350 KTPA acetic acid plant at Bharuch (INEOS licensing instead of the earlier JV idea). In Nov-2025 the CFO put BPA plus an upstream phenol plant at "roughly ₹7,000-8,000 cr". Decisions are expected by the end of 2026.
**Kearney:** the consultant identified ₹260-300 cr of yearly savings; by Feb-2026 only ₹5-7 cr had been realised, and management has not signed off a number. We include none of it beyond the CCPP.
**GMDC:** an MoU for underground coal gasification is at study stage; no capex attached yet.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we include the ₹2,800 cr list and the boiler (capex ₹1,600 / 800 / 500 cr in FY27-29E) and about ₹1,000 cr of extra chemicals revenue by FY29, a haircut to management's war-price estimate. We do not model BPA or phenol: at ₹7,000-8,000 cr it would absorb all the treasury and more, in a product (phenol/BPA) where Indian capacity is being added by others and Chinese supply sets the price. If approved, it is the single biggest risk to the cash that supports today's share price.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a protected TDI position, no pricing power

verdicts: Only producer in South Asia; ~60% of Indian demand; anti-dumping duties of US$102-440/t on imports.
Gives GNFC first call on Indian buyers, at import-parity prices.
Prices are set at import parity every one to three months; Chinese capacity and the rupee decide them.
Margins follow the cycle: 12% to 37% chemicals EBIT in five years.
Chinese TDI, aniline and acetic acid plants are several times larger and coal-based; TDI-II has not covered its fixed costs at FY25-26 prices.
The CCPP helps; scale cannot be fixed.
Own ammonia, nitric acids, CNA, syngas and power; fuel flexibility across oil, gas and coal.
Lets GNFC switch products as spreads move (e.g. TGU in Mar-2026).
Regulated returns; fixed costs and energy norms lag reality; loss every year since FY21.
Survives any downturn; the state decides how the cash is used.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** GNFC has a protected position in Indian TDI and the advantages of an integrated, debt-free complex, but no moat that protects profits. It is a price-taker against much larger Chinese producers in every chemical it sells, and its fertiliser business earns whatever the government allows. Pre-tax returns on operating capital of ~15% in FY26 (helped by the war) and ~6-9% in FY24-25 are the evidence.

sections.title: A boom, a bust and a war: ten years of earnings that follow chemical prices

blocks.p: GNFC's revenue was ₹4,552 cr in FY16 and ₹7,773 cr in FY26: about 5.5% a year, with almost all of the growth in one jump (FY22-23) when Chinese supply was disrupted after COVID. EBITDA (operating profit before other income) swung from ₹361 cr (FY17) to ₹2,384 cr (FY22) and back to ₹502 cr (FY24). Net profit followed: ₹1,710 cr at the FY22 peak, ₹497 cr in FY24 and ₹809 cr in FY26, of which ₹396 cr came in the single war-hit March quarter. The only loss in fifty years was FY15 (₹443 cr), the year TDI-II started on borrowed money.

pair.title: Revenue: one jump in FY22-23, flat since
EBITDA: ₹2,384 cr in FY22, ₹502 cr in FY24
EBITDA margin: 28% at the peak, 6% at the trough
Quarterly profit: the war doubled it

blocks.callout: **So what:** GNFC is a price-taker. Its profit is set by the gap between chemical prices (TDI, aniline, acetic acid, nitric acid) and feedstock costs (toluene, benzene, methanol, fuel oil, gas, coal), and Chinese supply sets both. Other income from its treasury (₹499 cr in FY26, 47% of pre-tax profit) steadies the bottom line. FY22-23 was a boom, FY24-25 a trough, and Q4FY26-Q1FY27 is a war spike: none of the three is a good base for valuation.

sections.title: Ten years of cash: debt repaid, a buyback, and ₹5,200 cr parked

blocks.p: Over FY17-26 GNFC generated ₹10,765 cr of operating cash. It spent only ₹2,153 cr on plants (it built nothing large between TDI-II in 2014 and the current projects), repaid ₹3,096 cr of debt, paid ₹1,714 cr of dividends and bought back ₹653 cr of shares in Dec-2023 at ₹770. The rest piled up: treasury (cash, deposits, G-secs, equity stakes and inter-corporate deposits) reached ~₹5,200 cr at March 2026, about ₹354 a share. Returns followed the chemical cycle: Screener's ROCE was 33% in FY22 and 12% in FY26 (diluted by the treasury); on operating capital alone the FY26 pre-tax return was ~15%, only slightly above a ~13% cost of equity, and that was helped by the war-time March quarter.

blocks.callout: **Capital allocation from here:** the cash is now being spent. ₹2,800 cr of projects (nitric acid, ammonium nitrate, an ammonia loop upgrade and a coal-fired steam and power plant) run to mid-2027, a ₹480-500 cr boiler follows, and management is studying BPA, polyols and a 350 KTPA acetic acid plant (BPA with an upstream phenol plant alone was put at ₹7,000-8,000 cr in Nov-2025). Meanwhile ₹2,410 cr sits in deposits with Gujarat State Financial Services, a state finance company, at ~7.25%. Minority shareholders get a 35-40% payout and no say in either decision.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean books, but other income is half of pre-tax profit

bullets: **Other income is half of pre-tax profit.** FY26 other income was ₹499 cr against PBT of ₹1,065 cr: interest ₹313 cr, dividends ₹24 cr, a non-cash government grant amortisation ₹61 cr (the deferred ASGP grant, ₹455 cr left), insurance ₹29 cr, FX ₹13 cr and miscellaneous ₹47 cr. In FY24 and FY25 other income was 72% and 63% of PBT.

**One-offs every year.** Management counted ~₹80 cr of one-time income in FY26 (insurance, urea freight escalation, catalyst-dust sale, a penalty from the CCPP contractor) and ~₹38 cr in FY25. FY27 will include ~₹61 cr of energy-norm arrears for FY26 and Q1FY27.
**Subsidy accounting.** Urea subsidy is booked on estimates of the normative cost and trued up later ("escalation/de-escalation"): +₹8 cr for earlier years in FY26, −₹35 cr in FY25.
**Inventory timing.** In Q1FY27 production ran ahead of sales at record prices; ~15% of that stock was sold by end-July at "mixed" realisations.
**Treasury classification.** ₹2,410 cr of ICDs with a state finance company sit in "loans and advances", so Screener's cash line understates treasury by that amount.
**Audit.** Suresh Surana & Associates (statutory) and K. G. Goyal (cost); clean opinions; simple structure (one associate, no subsidiaries of size).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN, with a quality caveat.** We found nothing aggressive. But headline EPS mixes three things: chemical spreads, treasury income and one-offs. Our estimates strip one-offs from other income (₹112 cr a year of non-treasury income, mostly the grant) and grow treasury income only with the cash balance.

sections.title: No debt and ₹354 a share of treasury, much of it outside Screener's cash line

blocks.p: GNFC has had no meaningful debt since FY21. Screener shows "cash and investments" of only ₹2,802 cr at March 2026, down from ₹4,612 cr, but that is a reclassification, not a loss: during FY26 the company moved ₹1,865 cr out of bank deposits and G-secs into inter-corporate deposits (ICDs) with Gujarat State Financial Services, which Screener records under "loans and advances". Adding them back, treasury rose slightly, to ~₹5,200 cr. About ₹1,000 cr of it is equity stakes in other Gujarat state companies (Gujarat Gas, Gujarat Alkalies, GSFC, Gujarat Chemical Port) and the GGRC associate, which earn dividends, not interest.

blocks.callout: **Working capital and subsidies:** fertiliser subsidy is paid by the government after sale, so subsidy receivables are the swing item. Total receivables were ₹1,413 cr (100 days of sales) in FY20 against ₹641 cr (30 days) in FY26; subsidy receivables were ₹496 cr at March 2026 and ~₹302 cr at December 2025, and the FY27 subsidy budget is ₹1.71 lakh cr. Our model holds net operating working capital at FY26's 1.6% of revenue, which includes that ₹496 cr. Each ₹500 cr of delayed subsidy would cost ~₹34 a share of treasury, not earnings.

sections.title: Ownership: the Government of Gujarat controls 41%; foreign funds have been selling

blocks.p: The Government of Gujarat controls GNFC through Gujarat State Investments (21.44%) and GSFC (19.86%), itself a state-controlled company: a 41.30% promoter group, unchanged for years, with no pledge. At June 2026 foreign portfolio investors held 13.11% (down from 20.1% in Dec-2023), domestic institutions 11.02% and the public 34.57%. In the March 2026 detail, mutual funds held 8.56% and resident individuals 27.37% across ~2.66 lakh shareholders. There is a small cross-holding: GNFC owns 75 lakh GSFC shares.

sections.title: The street: barely covered; the few calls we can find are Neutral

blocks.p: GNFC has almost no live sell-side coverage. We found no broker note dated July-September 2026 with a published target, method and estimates. A third-party blog (updated 11-Jun-2026) lists JM Financial at Neutral with ₹580 and ICICI Securities at Neutral with ₹550, without dates or methods; we could not find the notes themselves. The last full broker valuation we could read is HDFC Securities' stock note of Aug-2022 (base case ₹792 at 6.5x FY24E EPS), which shows how the street has valued GNFC: on P/E of one- to two-year-forward earnings, with no separate value for the cash. The stock rallied ~65% from its March-2026 low to ₹604 on 30-Sep-2026, so the market has moved well ahead of the Neutral calls.

blocks.callout: **What the cross-checks tell us.** EV/EBITDA (2x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,097 cr plus the Sep-28E treasury) gives ₹479, 16% above the P/E target: 2x is GNFC's own 2.0x median forward EV/EBITDA since 2021 leaving out FY24, FY25, FY26 (3.9x on all dates), cut by the −9% peer de-rating. That the market has paid only ~2-4x EBITDA for the operations once cash is netted off is the clearest sign of how little it trusts the use of that cash. The DCF (₹877) is more than double the target: it counts the ₹4,548 cr treasury at full value and assumes a 12% EBITDA margin and 5-13% revenue growth for fifteen years. The DCF is the value if the cash were returned and margins held at the long-run median; the P/E is what the market has actually paid. We side with the market's history, and show the gap.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a decent business at a war-time price

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's only TDI plant (~60% of the market) inside an integrated, debt-free Gujarat chemical complex, a loss-making regulated urea and ANP business, a small IT division, ₹5,200 cr of treasury and ₹2,800 cr of sensible brownfield projects that add ammonium nitrate capacity from mid-2027. All run by rotating state-appointed managers.

**What you are paying:** ₹604, or 8.6x war-time TTM EPS but 10.9x our Sep-28E EPS, against an 8.0x ex-trough history. On the street's method and our numbers the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).

bullets: **Rating: SELL, target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).** Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%.
**We would turn neutral below ~₹430** and buyers below ~₹360 on today's numbers, or sooner on evidence that the war premium is lasting (our bull case) or that cash is coming back to shareholders.
**Biggest swing factor:** the chemicals margin. Each 1 point is ~₹52 cr of EBIT in FY28E, ~₹2.6 of EPS and ~₹20 a share at 7.5x.

**Why not HOLD on the cash?** Because the treasury has been building for five years and the market has rarely paid for it (ex-trough, the operations have traded at ~2x EBITDA net of cash); our P/E derivation already reflects that history.

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: A chemical made from toluene and nitric acid, used to make flexible polyurethane foam (mattresses, furniture, car seats) and coatings.
Made from benzene and nitric acid; used for MDI (rigid foam), rubber chemicals and dyes.
Acetic acid is made from methanol and carbon monoxide ("carbonylation"); ethyl acetate is a solvent made from it.
Weak and concentrated nitric acid, made from ammonia; inputs for TDI, aniline and ammonium nitrate.
Ammonium nitrate solution, mainly for mining explosives.
Technical-grade urea; used to make diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) for BS6 trucks, plywood resins and cattle feed.
Fertiliser urea coated with neem oil; sold at a government-fixed price.
Ammonium nitro-phosphate: a fertiliser with 20% nitrogen and 20% phosphate.
The government schemes that pay urea makers a normative cost (gas, energy up to a norm, fixed costs) above the fixed farm price.
The energy per tonne of urea the government reimburses; energy used above it is the producer's loss.
A per-kg subsidy on N, P, K and S for complex fertilisers such as ANP, reset each Kharif (Apr-Sep) and Rabi (Oct-Mar) season.
The landed price of imports (world price + freight + duties); GNFC prices its chemicals off it.
An extra import duty on goods sold below fair value; India levies it on TDI from the EU, Saudi Arabia, China, Japan and Korea.
Inter-corporate deposit: a loan to another company. GSFS = Gujarat State Financial Services, a state finance company.
GNFC's coal-based captive steam and power plant at Dahej, replacing gas for TDI-II.
Segment profit before interest, unallocated items and tax (EBIT), including other income booked in the segment.
Cash, deposits, ICDs, G-secs and equity investments, less borrowings.
Half FY28E plus half FY29E: the 12-month-forward earnings the market will look at in September 2027.
